normalization.axes: glTF +Y up/+Z forward -> Blender import -> glTF export_yup; no extra axis rotation

parts.authoring: Blender-authored low-poly parts; paint x procedural noise grain, metal, roughness and the pennant's dye mask baked (Cycles CPU emission) into one atlas

materials.provenance: Base colour re-baked (Cycles CPU, emission, selected-to-active) from the approved TRELLIS source mesh onto fresh smart-projected UVs (the source atlas does not survive the cut and decimation) after the reconstructed wheels and the invented rear drawbar and ground post were cut away; no rear-view projection (the back, far side and underside are as TRELLIS invented them). Tangent normals baked from the source geometry and whiteout-blended with colour relief; AO baked from the decimated geometry; roughness derived from colour inside declared regions (the painted-black ward-glass panes are glossy; they are not transparent glass). Base colour lifted by luma power toneGamma (chroma ratios kept), set by eye, not calibrated against the concept. Base alpha opaque (never dyed). Artistic derivation, not measured PBR.

baseEncoding.reason: Base-colour alpha is the dye mask; libwebp's default lossy mode discards RGB under alpha 0.

settings.POSITION: SHORT normalized; one uniform scale per mesh folded into its node's scale (no offset), the inverse into its children
settings.TEXCOORD: UNSIGNED_SHORT normalized where the UVs lie in [0, 1]

reorder.method: meshoptimizer reorderMesh: vertex-cache triangle order, then vertex-fetch vertex order
reorder.check: a permutation: every vertex keeps its exact attribute bytes, and the triangles are the same, with the same winding, in another order

geometryCompression.check: every view decoded again: attribute views byte-identical to the reordered data; triangle index views hold the same triangles in the same order and winding (only the first vertex may rotate)

derivedFrom.note: The exact real-005-q-h output, reordered for locality and compressed by meshopt_glb.mjs (EXT_meshopt_compression, no lossy filters); the Blender cook was not re-run.
The exact real-005-q output (the shipped real-005-q-m before EXT_meshopt_compression) with its maps of 1024 px or more halved by resize_maps.py; the Blender cook was not re-run.
The exact real-005 output, quantized by quantize_static_glb.py; the Blender cook was not re-run.

cook.scriptsNote: SHA-256 of each script with LF line endings, equal to its copy in scripts/models/pipeline.
cook.verification: tests/wagon-models.test.ts checks the body, one spun node per axle whose rim touches the ground, the harness tips within 6 cm of the draft ox's hame hooks, the budgets, WebP maps and normals, and drives the wagon through the presenter without a DOM; tests/wagons-browser.test.ts decodes and renders it in the game's WebGL presenter.

textureResize.filter: 2x2 box to half size, as the GPU builds mip level 1: sRGB colour in linear light, alpha and data plainly
textureResize.reason: The game camera never samples this model's top mip level (follow camera at 18-40 m, 48 degree view, pixel ratio at most 1.75); halving its large maps leaves the game's frames unchanged and quarters their texture memory.

limitations: Single-view TRELLIS reconstruction from one approved concept: the far side, back and underside are TRELLIS's invention, with no rear-view painting projected onto them.
Roughness, metalness and ambient occlusion are derived from colour inside declared regions and Cycles bakes, not measured PBR or hand-painted masks.
One body mesh with its detail painted into a single base colour (cooked at 1024 px, shipped at 512 px); there are no LODs, trim sheets or separate material layers.
The base colour is lifted by luma power 0.85 (chroma kept), set by eye in review renders, not calibrated against the concept.
Re-cooking is not guaranteed to be byte-reproducible: MikkTSpace tangents can round differently on a few vertices, and Blender's smart UV project can lay out an atlas differently between runs.

The reconstructed wheels, drawbar and ground clutter were cut away and replaced by Blender-authored spoked wheels (1,972 triangles per axle node), shafts, crossbar, duga arch, warding bell and pennant with procedural wood grain: clean and sharper than the reconstructed body, and visibly a different kind of surface up close.

The TRELLIS texture atlas does not survive the cut and decimation (the first cooks showed smeared, streaked base colour), so the body is unwrapped afresh (smart UV project) and its base colour re-baked from the source mesh: detail is TRELLIS's 2048 px reconstruction resampled to 1024 px, shipped at 512 px.
The wooden parts' paint was sampled from the concept by eye; wheels and shafts are darker than the first cooks, which read far too light in game.
The pennant is a static rippled cloth (enlarged and rippled after the in-game review so it still reads from straight behind); it does not flutter, and the canvas and ropes do not move.
The body and wheels lean 0.085 rad about the centreline when disabled, as the procedural wagon did, so one rim lifts and the other sinks by up to about 8 cm.
The ward-glass panes are painted, glossy dark texture, not transparent or refractive glass.
A third cut removed a drawbar and ground post that TRELLIS invented behind the wagon; the back door and the rear sacks' far side are invented.

Allegiance reads only from the dyed pennant (teal friendly, stone neutral, red hostile) and the existing health-bar colour; the procedural wagon's slightly lighter canvas for a friendly shipment has no equivalent on the box body.
